A marksman is a general term to mean any soldier with good shooting proficiency. More recently, however, the role of a designated marksman or a platoon/company marksman has been more clearly defined. This role is distinct from a sniper.

A designated marksman is a squad level role. He moves with a member of the squad, and is expected to do everything they do. Just as every member of the squad has a specific role, however, so does the designated marksman. He's the guy who basically 'has deep'. His weapon, typically a semi-automatic rifle with a 3x-6x optic, allows effective engagement of targets up to 500–600 meters. Note the semi-automatic: for a designated marksman, absolute precision of a bolt action might not be necessary- given the shorter engagement ranges he's likely to be at, weight of fire and speed of target acquisition are necessary.

A platoon or company marksman are similar to a designated marksman, except that they are a platoon or company asset, much the same as a platoon has one machine gun team. Not all armies have them, and it's a matter of organisation. Similar to a designated marksman, they operate in small teams as part of an infantry unit. They don't necessarily operate as part of a squad, and will usually be part of the platoon or company's heavy weapons teams. They will usually have weapons one step up from the DM- they will be packing full blown semi auto sniper rifles like the dragunov SVD or sr-25,with engagement ranges out to 800m. The longest I was trained to shoot as a company marksman was about 700m. Their job will typically be to provide overwatch and precision fire support to the platoon or company, and eliminating high value targets. Think of them as mini-snipers

Sniper's are brigade or division assets- they are deployed to specific missions as needed and not every infantry unit has them. To put it simply, snipers are masters of all the skills an infantryman needs. Typically trained to a much higher degree than marksmen, snipers are principally scouts, and much of their training is focused on the silent movement, stalking, navigation, forward air and artillery control, and reconnaissance roles they will be expected to fulfill. Marksmen do not typically have this training, although they may develop it through experience. Snipers are expected to operate alone or in small teams with little or no support if the need arises. Snipers have a wide variety of missions, from reconnaissance, overwatch, destruction of high value targets, killing other snipers, and may even be attached to infantry units and act as marksmen. Due to their wide variety of roles, snipers may also sometimes be deployed behind enemy lines. Snipers are also armed with a larger variety of weapons, from semi-automatic sniper rifles, bolt action rifles, anti material rifles, and others, and may select their weapon based on the job.
